claims.scope: Repository implementation pattern only; not a claim that every repository already has this capability.
claims.statement: QIK-VRT implements bounded repository self-healing through exact state observation, typed technical blockers, isolated candidates and exact-head verification.

claims.scope: QIK-VRT governance rule and proposed safety principle; not a universal theorem.
claims.statement: Technical repair, external scientific evidence and external effect authorization must remain separate gates.

claims.scope: Definition used in this article; not an empirical law or an identity with biological fitness.
claims.statement: Connectability denotes the valid and verifiable successor states available while declared invariants remain satisfied.

claims.scope: Knowledge-representation proposal; domain completeness is not established.
claims.statement: A reusable idea can be stored as a versioned capsule containing context, assumptions, mechanism, evidence, limits, failures, interfaces and provenance.
Similarity makes an earlier idea a candidate for renewed validation, not an automatically valid transfer.

claims.scope: Collective intelligence means shared capacity to remember, test, compare and develop; not one group consciousness or automatic wisdom.
claims.statement: Provenance-bound contributions from many people, institutions and machines can form a shared socio-technical memory and a substrate for collective intelligence.

claims.scope: Cross-domain effectiveness and causal attribution remain untested here.
claims.statement: Whether this architecture measurably improves group performance across domains requires preregistered studies and independent replication.

claims.scope: Epistemic reinterpretation only; no physical retrocausality is asserted.
claims.statement: A later question can make an earlier preserved idea newly relevant without changing the earlier artifact or sending a physical signal backward in time.

claims.scope: Conceptual full sphere only; not empirical, physical or consensus-level completion.
claims.statement: The article reaches conceptual-architectural closure by joining self-healing, evidence preservation, idea reuse, collective memory, effect boundaries and temporal interpretation.

claims.scope: Empirical and physical completion is not established by this publication.
claims.statement: A scientifically and physically complete full sphere would additionally require domain-specific measurement, independent review, replication and non-circular correspondence to nature where physical claims are made.
